statedReasoning: This is a single-MP bill by Pavla Pivoňka Vaňková (STAN) amending zákon č. 117/1995 Sb., o státní sociální podpoře (State Social Support Act), specifically the parental benefit (rodičovský příspěvek) rules in § 30-31. Having now read the full bill text with explanatory report, the substantive changes are: (1) § 31 -- removes the 120-hour-per-month childcare/preschool attendance limit that previously disqualified a family from the 'personal all-day care' condition for claiming the benefit, and drops the related age-based attendance-tracking text as moot; (2) § 30 -- a one-off increase of the total parental-benefit cap from 350,000 Kč to 370,000 Kč, effective 1 Jan 2027, reflecting cumulative inflation since the last increase (1 Jan 2024); (3) new § 31a -- introduces an automatic annual valorization (indexation) mechanism: the government may raise the benefit by regulation (nařízení vlády, not by further legislation) each 1 January whenever cumulative CPI growth over the tracked period reaches at least 5%, rounded up to the nearest thousand Kč. The stated rationale (Part 1-3 of the DZ) is to prevent real-value erosion of the benefit from inflation and avoid disruptive 'jump' increases that a 2022 IDEA/CERGE-EI study found harm family predictability and prolong benefit uptake, especially among university-educated women. The DZ states an estimated fiscal impact of ~375-440M Kč in year 1, ~750-880M Kč in year 2, and ~1-1.1bn Kč/year at full ramp-up in year 3, no impact on other public budgets, no identified corruption risk, and no lobbying activity. Effective date proposed: 1 Jan 2027.
researchedContext: The graph's recorded amended law (117/1995 Sb.) matches the fresh body-text census exactly -- amendedLawsRealFromCensus shows realLaws=[117/1995], recordedLaws=[117/1995], undercount=0. This is a single-subject MP bill, not an omnibus, so no undercount is expected and none was found; this is consistent, not a data-quality finding. Legislative history independently confirms the government returned a formal negative opinion (nesouhlas, tisk 112/1) on 18 Mar 2026, but the bill nonetheless proceeded to committee (Social Policy Committee as guarantor) on 2 Apr 2026 -- the content of that negative opinion itself was not accessible and is not characterized here. A web search separately surfaced an unrelated, more prominent government bill (tisk 198, a parental-benefit increase) on which the same MP also spoke publicly in July 2026 -- that is a distinct print and its content is not conflated with tisk 112 here.

No graph-sourced conflict signal exists to assess, and I found no independent evidence of a financial tie for the sole submitter. The bill's own corruption-risk assessment (section 10 of the DZ) states no corruption impact and no lobbying was identified. Honest finding: no conflict indicator present.
